CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman for: security warnings, irreversible action confirmations, multi-step sequences where fragment order risks misread, user asks to clarify or repeats question. Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

Missing CI environment variable guardrail check
Medium Severity

MaybeAutoUpdate and CanPromptInteractively never check the CI environment variable, despite both the PR description and the new auto-update.md documentation explicitly listing it as a guardrail. On CI runners that happen to have /dev/tty available (self-hosted runners, some Docker configs), the interactive huh prompt will fire and hang the pipeline waiting for input.

1	// Package interactive provides TTY-related helpers shared between the cli
2	// and strategy packages without inducing an import cycle (strategy cannot
3	// import cli).
4	package interactive
5	
6	import "os"
7	
8	// CanPromptInteractively checks if /dev/tty is available for interactive prompts.
9	// Returns false when running as an agent subprocess (no controlling terminal).
10	//
11	// In test environments, ENTIRE_TEST_TTY overrides the real check:
12	//   - ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1 → simulate human (TTY available)
13	//   - ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0 → simulate agent (no TTY)
14	func CanPromptInteractively() bool {
15		if v := os.Getenv("ENTIRE_TEST_TTY"); v != "" {
16			return v == "1"
17		}
18	
19		// Gemini CLI sets GEMINI_CLI=1 when running shell commands.
20		// Gemini subprocesses may have access to the user's TTY, but they can't
21		// actually respond to interactive prompts. Treat them as non-TTY.
22		// See: https://geminicli.com/docs/tools/shell/
23		if os.Getenv("GEMINI_CLI") != "" {
24			return false
25		}
26	
27		// Copilot CLI sets COPILOT_CLI=1 when running hook subprocesses (v0.0.421+).
28		// Like Gemini, the subprocess may inherit the user's TTY but can't respond
29		// to interactive prompts.
30		if os.Getenv("COPILOT_CLI") != "" {
31			return false
32		}
33	
34		// Pi Coding Agent sets PI_CODING_AGENT=true when running shell commands.
35		// Like other agents, the subprocess may inherit the TTY but can't respond
36		// to interactive prompts.
37		if os.Getenv("PI_CODING_AGENT") != "" {
38			return false
39		}
40	
41		// GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 disables git's own terminal prompts.
42		// Factory AI Droid (and other non-interactive environments like CI) set this.
43		// Since we run as a git hook, respect it — if the environment doesn't want
44		// git prompting, our hook shouldn't prompt either.
45		if os.Getenv("GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT") == "0" {
46			return false
47		}
48	
49		tty, err := os.OpenFile("/dev/tty", os.O_RDWR, 0)
50		if err != nil {
51			return false
52		}
53		_ = tty.Close()
54		return true
55	}

1	package versioncheck
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"errors"
6		"fmt"
7		"io"
8		"os"
9		"os/exec"
10		"runtime"

13	
14		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/interactive"
15		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
16	)

18	// envKillSwitch disables the interactive update prompt regardless of TTY.
19	const envKillSwitch = "ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE"
20	
21	// Test seams.
22	var (
23		runInstaller  = realRunInstaller
24		confirmUpdate = realConfirmUpdate
25	)
26	
27	// MaybeAutoUpdate offers an interactive upgrade after the standard
28	// "version available" notification has been printed. Silent on every
29	// failure path — it must never interrupt the CLI.
30	func MaybeAutoUpdate(ctx context.Context, w io.Writer, currentVersion string) {
31		if os.Getenv(envKillSwitch) != "" {
32			return
33		}
34		if !interactive.CanPromptInteractively() {
35			return
36		}
37	
38		confirmed, err := confirmUpdate()
39		if err != nil {
40			logging.Debug(ctx, "auto-update: prompt failed", "error", err.Error())
41			return
42		}
43		if !confirmed {
44			return
45		}
46	
47		cmdStr := updateCommand(currentVersion)
48		fmt.Fprintf(w, "\nUpdating Entire CLI: %s\n", cmdStr)
49		if err := runInstaller(ctx, cmdStr); err != nil {
50			fmt.Fprintf(w, "Update failed: %v\n", err)
51			return
52		}
53		fmt.Fprintln(w, "Update complete. Re-run entire to use the new version.")
54	}
55	
56	func realConfirmUpdate() (bool, error) {
57		// Pre-select "Yes" so pressing Enter accepts — matches the (Y/n) UX.
58		confirmed := true
59		form := huh.NewForm(
60			huh.NewGroup(
61				huh.NewConfirm().
62					Title("Install the new version now?").
63					Affirmative("Yes").
64					Negative("No").
65					Value(&confirmed),
66			),
67		).WithTheme(huh.ThemeDracula())
68		if os.Getenv("ACCESSIBLE") != "" {
69			form = form.WithAccessible(true)
70		}
71		if err := form.Run(); err != nil {
72			if errors.Is(err, huh.ErrUserAborted) || errors.Is(err, huh.ErrTimeout) {
73				return false, nil
74			}
75			return false, fmt.Errorf("confirm form: %w", err)
76		}
77		return confirmed, nil
78	}
79	
80	// realRunInstaller shells out to the installer command, streaming stdin/stdout/stderr
81	// so password prompts and progress output reach the user.
82	func realRunInstaller(ctx context.Context, cmdStr string) error {
83		var c *exec.Cmd
84		if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
85			c = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "cmd", "/C", cmdStr)
86		} else {
87			c = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "sh", "-c", cmdStr)
88		}
89		c.Stdin = os.Stdin
90		c.Stdout = os.Stdout
91		c.Stderr = os.Stderr
92		if err := c.Run(); err != nil {
93			return fmt.Errorf("installer exited: %w", err)
94		}
95		return nil
96	}

# Ship Changes

Commit current changes, push to remote, and update the PR.

## Step 1: Analyze changes

1. Run `git diff --stat` and `git diff` to understand what changed
2. Run `git status` to see untracked files
3. Run `git log --oneline -3` to match the repo's commit message style

## Step 2: Commit

1. Stage only the relevant changed/untracked files by name (never `git add -A` or `git add .`)
2. Write a concise commit message that focuses on the "why" not the "what"
   - If `` is provided, use it as the commit message
   - Otherwise, draft one from the diff
3. Commit. If hooks fail, diagnose and fix — do NOT use `--no-verify`

## Step 3: Push

1. Check if the branch tracks a remote: `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{u}`
2. If not tracking, push with `-u origin <branch>`
3. If tracking, just `git push`
4. If push is rejected (remote has new commits), pull with rebase first then push

## Step 4: Update PR

1. Find the open PR for the current branch: `gh pr view --json number,body,title`
2. If no PR exists, skip this step and inform the user
3. Compare the current PR body against the new changes:
   - If the changes are within the existing PR scope, update the description to reflect the current state
   - If the changes are additive or a follow-up, add a PR comment summarizing what was just pushed instead
4. When updating the PR body, preserve the overall structure but refresh the summary bullets and test plan
5. When adding a comment, keep it concise — bullet points of what changed and why
6. **Before making any PR update (description edit or comment), show the user the exact text you plan to post and ask for their approval. Do NOT post until they confirm.**

## Rules

- Never commit files that look like secrets (.env, credentials, tokens)
- Never force push
- Always show the user what was committed and the PR URL when done

Pushed `fc3d0e3c5` to `auto-update`. PR #997: https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/997

PR body already lists `CI` guardrail + "CI gate" test in test plan — this commit just backs those claims with real code. No description update needed. Want me to post a short comment noting the CI env check is now implemented?

---

Re cache-vs-install-failure:

Agree with your call. Fetch-failure path already silent (no prompt, no cache bump) — rate-limit/gh-down never nags user, never locks them out.

Install-failure path: cache bumped before prompt runs. If `brew upgrade` fails (network mid-install, sudo denied, etc.), user waits 24h or runs command manually. Tradeoff:

- Reset-on-failure = re-prompt every invocation until success → noisy if the install reliably fails (e.g. no brew on PATH, sudo required in non-sudo context)
- Keep-as-is = one shot per day, user sees the exact command printed (`Updating Entire CLI: brew upgrade --cask entire`) and can run it themselves

Current behavior is the right default. If you want a middle ground later: reset cache only on transient errors (network, 5xx) and keep cache on permanent errors (command not found, permission denied) — but that's a classification problem and probably not worth the code. Leave as-is.

input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Invalidate version-check cache when installer fails

Previously the 24h cache was bumped before the installer ran, so if
`brew upgrade` / `mise upgrade` / `scoop update` failed (network loss
mid-install, auth, etc.), the user had to wait a full day for the
auto-update prompt to re-arm.

MaybeAutoUpdate now reports installer failure back to CheckAndNotify,
which zeros LastCheckTime so the next CLI invocation re-fetches and
re-prompts. Fetch-failure behavior (cache still bumped to avoid
hammering GitHub during outages) is unchanged.
EOF
)"

message.content: what happens if the user says NO to upgrade? when do we display the message next time ?

content.text:
Flow when user declines:

1. `CheckAndNotify` loads cache, fetches latest version, bumps `LastCheckTime = time.Now()` **before** prompting (`versioncheck.go:64`)
2. `MaybeAutoUpdate` shows prompt, user picks No, returns `installerFailed=false`
3. Since `installerFailed=false`, cache is **not** rolled back
4. Next CLI invocation: if `time.Since(cache.LastCheckTime) < 24h` → `CheckAndNotify` returns immediately at `versioncheck.go:51`. No notification, no prompt.

So: **re-prompt happens on the first CLI invocation after 24h elapsed** since the decline. Until then: total silence — no notification banner, no prompt, no fetch.

Kill switch `ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` opts out permanently (per-invocation env var). There's no persisted "never ask again" option.

Research how popular CLIs handle auto-update / version-upgrade prompts. I'm specifically interested in the UX for "user was notified a new version is available and declined (or ignored)" — when do they re-prompt? Do they have per-version suppression, never-ask-again flags, periodic re-nag intervals, skip-this-version options, etc.

Please investigate the actual behavior (code or docs) of at least:

1. **Stripe CLI** (`stripe`) — check https://github.com/stripe/stripe-cli source; look for "version check", "update available", skip/defer logic.
2. **OpenAI Codex CLI** (`codex`) — check https://github.com/openai/codex; look at how it handles "new version available" and auto-update opt-in/out.
3. **GitHub CLI** (`gh`) — well-documented; look at the version-check cadence and any "don't ask again" behavior (it just prints a banner, AFAIK; confirm).
4. **npm** — the `update-notifier` library that most Node CLIs use — has interesting knobs: defer, skipVersion config key, weekly vs daily intervals.
5. **Claude Code CLI** (if you can find public docs/source) — how it handles version drift.

For each, report back in 6-10 lines:
- Does it prompt interactively, or just print a banner?
- After decline/ignore, when is the user reminded again (next invocation? next day? next version? never until opt-in?)
- Is there a "skip this version" / "never ask again" mechanism?
- What's the cache/state file look like (if documented)?

Then give a 3-4 line synthesis recommending what you think Entire CLI should do. Context: Entire currently (a) prints a banner once per 24h, (b) if outdated, prompts Y/N to run the installer, (c) if user picks No, stays silent for 24h (same as if they'd never been prompted), (d) if installer fails, invalidates cache to re-prompt next invocation, (e) kill-switch env var `ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` is the only "never" option.

Keep the final report under 400 words. Accuracy > breadth — if you can't verify a CLI's behavior, say so rather than guess.

lastPrompt: How other like stripe or codex handles it?

content.text:
I have enough to write a verified report. Let me also confirm codex's dismissal logic once more: codex stores `dismissed_version` in `~/.codex/version.json`, and `get_upgrade_version_for_popup` suppresses the popup only when `dismissed_version == latest_version`. So a NEW version ignores the dismissal. That's the key nuance.

Here's the report:

---

## Research: CLI update-prompt UX

**1. Stripe CLI** — Verified via `pkg/version/version.go`. Non-interactive **banner only**: prints "A newer version of the Stripe CLI is available" on every invocation where `Version != "master"` and the GitHub latest release differs. No caching, no state file, no skip/dismiss mechanism, no "don't ask again" — just a flat one-line print every run. Very minimal. (`/tmp` not used; source fetched from GitHub API.)

**2. OpenAI Codex CLI** — Verified via `codex-rs/tui/src/update_prompt.rs` and `updates.rs`. **Interactive TUI popup** with three options: `Update now`, `Not now`, `Don't remind`. State file: `~/.codex/version.json` with `{latest_version, last_checked_at, dismissed_version}`. Background check runs if `last_checked_at > 20h` ago. "Not now" re-prompts on every subsequent invocation. "Don't remind" persists `dismissed_version = <current latest>`; the popup is suppressed **only while latest == dismissed** — when a newer release ships, the dismissal is effectively ignored and the user is prompted again. This is per-version suppression, not "never again."

**3. GitHub CLI (`gh`)** — Verified via `internal/update/update.go` and `internal/ghcmd/cmd.go`. **Banner only, no prompt.** Prints "A new release of gh is available: x → y" on stderr after the command runs. 24h state cache at `state.yml` with `checked_for_update_at` + `latest_release`. No skip-this-version or dismiss mechanism — only opt-outs: `GH_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER` env var, CI detection, and non-TTY suppression. Homebrew users are deliberately silenced for recent releases (so the tap has time to catch up).

content.text:
Summary of what other CLIs do:

| CLI | Style | On decline / ignore |
|-----|-------|---------------------|
| **Stripe** | Banner only, every run | Banner every run forever |
| **GitHub (`gh`)** | Banner only, 24h cache | Silent 24h, then banner again |
| **npm (`update-notifier`)** | Banner only, 24h cache | Silent 24h; opt-out via env/config; no per-version skip |
| **OpenAI Codex** | **Interactive popup** with 3 options: Update now / Not now / Don't remind | "Not now" → re-prompt every run. "Don't remind" → persists `dismissed_version`, suppressed until a **newer** release ships |
| **Claude Code** | Silent background auto-update (native install) or no-op (brew) | No prompt at all |

Entire's current behavior (24h silent after decline) is between `gh` and Codex.

**Closest comparable is Codex** since we also do an interactive prompt. Their best idea is the **per-version dismiss**: declining suppresses the prompt for that exact version, but a newer version re-arms it automatically. Avoids the "I already told you no yesterday, stop asking" UX without a true `never ask again` footgun.

If you want to match that, we'd:
1. Add a third option to the prompt (`Yes` / `No` / `Skip this version`)
2. Store `dismissed_version` in the existing `~/.config/entire/version_check.json`
3. Suppress prompt while `latest_version == dismissed_version`; auto-re-prompt when `latest_version` moves past it

`ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` stays as the hard kill. Want me to implement it?

Simplify auto-update decline/failure UX

Revert the cache-invalidation-on-installer-failure branch and keep the
24h window uniform for every terminal state:

- User declines → silent for 24h (unchanged).
- User accepts and installer succeeds → no re-prompt until the next
  outdated release is detected 24h later (unchanged).
- User accepts and installer fails → print the failure plus a manual
  retry hint ("Try again later with: <installer command>") and stay
  silent for 24h. Avoids re-prompting every invocation while an upstream
  issue (network, auth, repo outage) is still in place; the user has
  the exact command to retry manually when ready.

Drops the now-unused installerFailed return value from MaybeAutoUpdate
and the corresponding cache-reset path in CheckAndNotify. Matches the
simpler "every failure path keeps the 24h cache fresh" invariant (only
a fetch failure leaves the cache fresh as before, same as accept/decline
paths).
EOF
)"

1	//go:build integration && unix
2	
3	package integration
4	
5	import (
6		"fmt"
7		"os"
8		"path/filepath"
9		"strings"
10		"testing"
11		"time"
12	)
13	
14	// RunResumeInteractive executes the resume command with a pty, allowing
15	// interactive prompt responses. The respond function receives the pty for
16	// reading output and writing input. See RunCommandInteractive for details.
17	func (env *TestEnv) RunResumeInteractive(branchName string, respond func(ptyFile *os.File) string) (string, error) {
18		env.T.Helper()
19		return env.RunCommandInteractive([]string{"resume", branchName}, respond)
20	}
21	
22	// TestResume_LocalLogNewerTimestamp_UserConfirmsOverwrite tests that when the user
23	// confirms the overwrite prompt interactively, the local log is replaced.
24	func TestResume_LocalLogNewerTimestamp_UserConfirmsOverwrite(t *testing.T) {
25		t.Parallel()
26		env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t)
27	
28		// Create a session with a specific timestamp
29		session := env.NewSession()
30		if err := env.SimulateUserPromptSubmit(session.ID); err != nil {
31			t.Fatalf("SimulateUserPromptSubmit failed: %v", err)
32		}
33	
34		content := "def hello; end"
35		env.WriteFile("hello.rb", content)
36	
37		session.CreateTranscript(
38			"Create hello method",
39			[]FileChange{{Path: "hello.rb", Content: content}},
40		)
41		if err := env.SimulateStop(session.ID, session.TranscriptPath); err != nil {
42			t.Fatalf("SimulateStop failed: %v", err)
43		}
44	
45		// Commit the session's changes (manual-commit requires user to commit)
46		env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Create hello method", "hello.rb")
47	
48		featureBranch := env.GetCurrentBranch()
49	
50		// Create a local log with a NEWER timestamp than the checkpoint
51		if err := os.MkdirAll(env.ClaudeProjectDir, 0o755); err != nil {
52			t.Fatalf("failed to create Claude project dir: %v", err)
53		}
54		existingLog := filepath.Join(env.ClaudeProjectDir, session.ID+".jsonl")
55		futureTimestamp := time.Now().Add(24 * time.Hour).UTC().Format(time.RFC3339)
56		newerContent := fmt.Sprintf(`{"type":"human","timestamp":"%s","message":{"content":"newer local work"}}`, futureTimestamp)
57		if err := os.WriteFile(existingLog, []byte(newerContent), 0o644); err != nil {
58			t.Fatalf("failed to write existing log: %v", err)
59		}
60	
61		// Switch to main
62		env.GitCheckoutBranch(masterBranch)
63	
64		// Resume interactively and confirm the overwrite
65		output, err := env.RunResumeInteractive(featureBranch, func(ptyFile *os.File) string {
66			out, promptErr := WaitForPromptAndRespond(ptyFile, "[y/N]", "y\n", 10*time.Second)
67			if promptErr != nil {
68				t.Logf("Warning: %v", promptErr)
69			}
70			return out
71		})
72		if err != nil {
73			t.Fatalf("resume with user confirmation failed: %v\nOutput: %s", err, output)
74		}
75	
76		// Verify local log was overwritten with checkpoint content
77		data, err := os.ReadFile(existingLog)
78		if err != nil {
79			t.Fatalf("failed to read log: %v", err)
80		}
81		if strings.Contains(string(data), "newer local work") {
82			t.Errorf("local log should have been overwritten after user confirmed, but still has newer content: %s", string(data))
83		}
84		if !strings.Contains(string(data), "Create hello method") {
85			t.Errorf("restored log should contain checkpoint transcript, got: %s", string(data))
86		}
87	}
88	
89	// TestResume_LocalLogNewerTimestamp_UserDeclinesOverwrite tests that when the user
90	// declines the overwrite prompt interactively, the local log is preserved.
91	func TestResume_LocalLogNewerTimestamp_UserDeclinesOverwrite(t *testing.T) {
92		t.Parallel()
93		env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t)

87	// WaitForPromptAndRespond reads from the pty until it sees the expected prompt text,
88	// then writes the response. Returns the output read so far.
89	func WaitForPromptAndRespond(ptyFile *os.File, promptSubstring, response string, timeout time.Duration) (string, error) {
90		var output bytes.Buffer
91		buf := make([]byte, 1024)
92		deadline := time.Now().Add(timeout)
93	
94		for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
95			// Set read deadline to avoid blocking forever
96			_ = ptyFile.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(100 * time.Millisecond))
97			n, err := ptyFile.Read(buf)
98			if n > 0 {
99				output.Write(buf[:n])
100				if strings.Contains(output.String(), promptSubstring) {
101					// Found the prompt, send response
102					_, _ = ptyFile.WriteString(response)
103					return output.String(), nil
104				}
105			}
106			if err != nil && !os.IsTimeout(err) {
107				return output.String(), err
108			}
109		}
110		return output.String(), fmt.Errorf("timeout waiting for prompt containing %q", promptSubstring)
111	}

Matches the fix pattern from commit `1d1e01296`. Local integration suite with `CI=true` passes in 116s. Waiting on CI to confirm.

#!/bin/sh
#MISE description="Build the CLI"

TAG=$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 || echo "v0.0.0")
COMMIT=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
VERSION="${TAG}-dev-${COMMIT}"

OUTPUT="entire"
case "$(uname -s)" in MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*|Windows_NT) OUTPUT="entire.exe" ;; esac

go build -ldflags "-X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioninfo.Version=${VERSION} -X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioninfo.Commit=${COMMIT}" -o "$OUTPUT" ./cmd/entire

content.text:
## Manual test steps for auto-update prompt

### Setup — build a CLI that thinks it's old

```bash
go build -ldflags "-X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioninfo.Version=0.1.0" -o /tmp/entire-old ./cmd/entire
```

GitHub's latest release is much newer than `0.1.0`, so every run thinks an upgrade is available.

### Reset 24h cache between each scenario

```bash
rm -f ~/.config/entire/version_check.json
```

Always do this before each scenario — otherwise the 24h cache short-circuits the whole flow.

---

### Scenario 1 — Happy path, user accepts

```bash
rm -f ~/.config/entire/version_check.json
/tmp/entire-old status
```

Expect: banner → `Install the new version now? [Yes/No]` → press Enter / `y` → installer command is printed → your real `brew upgrade --cask entire` runs. **Caution:** this will actually upgrade you to the real latest. Run `brew upgrade --cask entire@nightly` skip or just switch to scenario 2/3 if you don't want the real upgrade.

### Scenario 2 — User declines

```bash
rm -f ~/.config/entire/version_check.json
/tmp/entire-old status
# press "n" at the prompt
```

Expect: prompt vanishes, no install, cache file now exists. Second invocation: total silence for 24h.

```bash
/tmp/entire-old status   # no banner, no prompt
```

### Scenario 3 — User accepts but installer fails (safe, no real upgrade)

Override `updateCommand` at runtime by pointing the installer-manager lookup at a fake executable. Easiest without code changes: build with a fake `PATH`:

```bash
rm -f ~/.config/entire/version_check.json
mkdir -p /tmp/bad-path
cat > /tmp/bad-path/brew <<'SH'
#!/bin/sh
echo "simulated brew failure" >&2
exit 1
SH
chmod +x /tmp/bad-path/brew
PATH=/tmp/bad-path:$PATH /tmp/entire-old status
# press "y"
```

Expect:
```
Updating Entire CLI: brew upgrade --cask entire
simulated brew failure
Update failed: installer exited: exit status 1
Try again later with: brew upgrade --cask entire
```

Verify cache still bumped (no re-prompt for 24h):
```bash
cat ~/.config/entire/version_check.json
PATH=/tmp/bad-path:$PATH /tmp/entire-old status   # silent — cache held
```

### Scenario 4 — Kill switch

```bash
rm -f ~/.config/entire/version_check.json
ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 /tmp/entire-old status
```

Expect: banner prints, **no prompt**. Cache still bumped.

### Scenario 5 — CI guardrail

```bash
rm -f ~/.config/entire/version_check.json
CI=true /tmp/entire-old status
```

Expect: banner prints, **no prompt** (CanPromptInteractively returns false before reaching the prompt). Same effect as scenario 4 but via different guardrail.

### Scenario 6 — Non-TTY (pipe)

```bash
rm -f ~/.config/entire/version_check.json
/tmp/entire-old status | cat
```

Expect: banner (or nothing, depending on stdout buffering), **no prompt** (no TTY).

---

### Tips

- Banner text comes from `printNotification` in `versioncheck.go`; prompt comes from `MaybeAutoUpdate` in `autoupdate.go`
- Check the cache file to understand state: `cat ~/.config/entire/version_check.json`
- To force the prompt command to be a specific string without touching your install, edit `updateCommand` temporarily or set `executablePath` test seam (not wired to env, would need a small patch)

Want me to add a hidden `entire debug auto-update` subcommand that does scenario 3 without needing PATH manipulation? It would call `MaybeAutoUpdate` directly with a configurable fake installer.

Right — you're on fish; heredoc (`<<'JSON' ... JSON`) is bash/zsh syntax. Fish-compatible:

```fish
mkdir -p /tmp/mock-gh
echo '{"tag_name":"v99.0.0","prerelease":false}' > /tmp/mock-gh/release.json
```

```fish
printf '%s\n' '{"tag_name":"v99.0.0","prerelease":false}' > /tmp/mock-gh/release.json
```

Verify:

```fish
cat /tmp/mock-gh/release.json
```

Continuing the recipe:

### 3. Serve it

```fish
cd /tmp/mock-gh; and python3 -m http.server 8765 &
```

### 4. Point the CLI at the mock and test

```fish
rm -f ~/.config/entire/version_check.json
env ENTIRE_VERSION_CHECK_URL=http://localhost:8765/release.json /tmp/entire-old status
```

Expect: banner (`v0.1.0 → v99.0.0`), prompt, no GitHub hit. Change `tag_name` in `release.json` to whatever you want to simulate.

### Stop the mock server

```fish
kill %1
```

(no cache touched)"]) dev -- no --> cache{"cache age < 24h?"} cache -- yes --> skip cache -- no --> fetch["fetch GitHub /releases/latest
(2s timeout)"] fetch --> bump["cache.LastCheckTime := now()
saveCache()"] bump --> fok{fetch succeeded?} fok -- no --> done24 fok -- yes --> outdated{isOutdated?} outdated -- no --> done24 outdated -- yes --> banner["print banner:

(CI=true, no /dev/tty, agent subprocess)" --> done24 tty -- true --> prompt["huh prompt:
'Install the new version now?'"] prompt --> ans{user answer} ans -- No --> done24 ans -- Yes --> run["run installer command
(brew / mise / scoop / curl)"] run --> res{installer exit code} res -- 0 --> ok["print:
'Update complete. Re-run entire to use the new version.'"] res -- "non-zero" --> fail["print:
'Update failed: <err>'
'Try again later running:'
' <installer cmd>'"] ok --> done24 fail --> done24 done24(["24h cache is fresh
no re-prompt until it expires"]) ``` **Invariants:** - Every path that reaches the fetch step bumps the 24h cache — declining, a failed fetch, a "not outdated" result, a no-TTY exit, and a failed installer all look the same to the cache. | Option | Wording |
